target_customer: General contractors, mining and construction firms with existing heavy equipment fleets
problem: Heavy equipment operators are scarce and machines sit idle, and buying new autonomous vehicles is costly, so retrofitting existing machines for supervised autonomy is attractive.
business_model: Retrofit hardware and software sold or leased through equipment dealers and direct to contractors
product_category: Supervised autonomy and teleoperation for heavy equipment

founders.name: Vinay Shet
education: PhD in computer science, University of Maryland, College Park
founders.background_notes: YC page: Director of Product Management at Lyft on self-driving, earlier product lead for Google Street View, Maps and reCAPTCHA.

founders.name: Rom Clement
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked on self-driving at Lyft L5 and on Google Street View.

competitors.name: Built Robotics
competitors.traction_then: over 100 million dollars in customer commitments claimed
competitors.funding_then: 33 million dollar Series B in September 2019, 48 million dollars total

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrofitting varied machines with sensors, remote control and supervised autonomy demands robotics and safety engineering across hardware makes.

defensibility.rationale: Retrofit integrations and dealer partnerships were hard to copy, but several rivals such as Built Robotics and SafeAI pursued similar goals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: John Deere added Teleo to its 2021 startup collaborator program rather than copying it, and Havoc acquired it in March 2026.

market_need_then: Construction labor shortages and the cost of new autonomous machines made retrofitting existing fleets appealing, though no dated spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Started at teleo.ai, an exact match name on the .ai domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and pragmatic, an incremental pathway to full autonomy

branding.community_and_virality: Won a 2022 Bay Area Inno award per the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name and trade press coverage, but no sourced brand identity or community, and search confuses it with Teneo.ai.

outcome_analysis: Teleo's founders came from Lyft Level 5 and Google, and it raised a 12 million dollar Series A in June 2022 led by UP.Partners plus a 16.2 million dollar extension in 2024, about 29.8 million dollars total per the Robot Report. It sold through John Deere dealers and contractors with a retrofit approach. Havoc acquired it in March 2026 alongside drone maker Mavrik with terms undisclosed, a defense autonomy consolidation rather than a clear venture return.
notes: Series A extension investors and exact month come from search result snippets of the Robot Report and AVI, only partly opened. A City Biz item lists Y Combinator as a Series A lead; no other source says so, so it is not recorded. The Havoc deal date of March 11, 2026 comes from search summaries of the press release.
